new_today.title: COBRA: Cell-type-specific Orthogonal Batch effect Removal Algorithm in single cell RNA-sequencing data.
new_today.title_zh: COBRA：单细胞RNA测序数据中细胞类型特异性正交批次效应去除算法。
new_today.summary_zh: 单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）能够高分辨率分析细胞异质性，但批次效应仍是数据整合中的关键挑战。现有批次校正方法通常假设批次效应在不同细胞类型间均匀，在降维空间中操作可能导致生物信息丢失，且需要大量计算资源。这里我们介绍COBRA，一种基于线性模型的批次校正方法，显式调整细胞类型特异性批次效应。通过将批次相关参数与生物变量正交化，COBRA去除技术伪影，同时保留有意义的转录差异。当细胞类型注释不可用时，COBRA实现迭代聚类算法来估计伪细胞类型，同时考虑批次效应。COBRA保留完整基因表达矩阵，确保下游分析无缝整合。我们在模拟和真实数据集（包括2型糖尿病和COVID-19数据集）上评估了COBRA。COBRA在批次混合效率、生物组结构保留和差异表达基因检测准确性方面表现更优。COBRA可在https://github.com/wonlab-healthstat/COBRA免费获取。复

extra.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution profiling of cellular heterogeneity, yet batch effects remain a critical challenge in data integration. Existing batch correction methods often assume homogeneous batch effect across cell types, operate in reduced-dimensional space leading to potential loss of biological information, and require extensive computational resources. Here, we introduce COBRA, a linear model-based batch correction method that explicitly adjusts cell-type-specific batch effect. By orthogonalizing batch-associated parameters with respect to biological variables, COBRA removes technical artifacts while preserving biologically meaningful transcriptional differences. When cell type annotations are unavailable, COBRA implements an iterative clustering algorithm to estimate pseudo-cell types while accounting for batch effects. COBRA retains the full gene expression matrix, ensuring seamless integration for downstream analyses. We evaluated COBRA across simulated and real-world datasets, including type 2 diabetes and COVID-19 datasets. COBRA outperformed in terms of batch mixing efficiency, preservation of biological group structure, and accuracy of differentially expressed gene detection. COBRA is freely available at https://github.com/wonlab-healthstat/COBRA. The code to reproduce the analyses is archived at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19891355). Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

new_today.title: Uncovering Cellular Resolution in scRNAseq via Unbiased Cell and Gene Network Analysis
new_today.title_zh: 通过无偏细胞和基因网络分析揭示scRNAseq中的细胞分辨率
new_today.summary_zh: 单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）数据的常规注释严重依赖手动、基于标记的阈值设定，这种方法可能掩盖细微的转录梯度，并将功能不同的细胞状态合并为广泛异质群体。这里我们将高斯多图模型（GmGM）框架应用于10x Genomics PBMC数据集，该框架从单个scRNA-seq数据矩阵联合推断细胞-细胞和基因-基因依赖结构。十次独立的GMGM-Leiden聚类运行通过软聚类集成方法整合为稳健的共识分区，并与参考细胞类型注释进行基准比较。该策略产生稳定的聚类分区，能解析参考注释未区分的生物学意义亚群。同时，对每个聚类，通过跨分辨率共识Leiden聚类从拟合模型中提取基因共表达模块，使用标准网络指标评估，并通过网络富集分析测试（NEAT）进行功能验证，确认非随机富集信号。模块评分程序将网络拓扑与每细胞、每聚类表达特征联系起来，并展示了GmGM的新扩展，在单次模型运行中恢复共享细胞-细胞网络和群体

extra.description: Conventional annotation of single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data relies heavily on manual, marker-based thresholding, an approach that can obscure subtle transcriptomic gradients and collapse functionally distinct cell states into broad, heterogeneous populations. Here we apply the Gaussian multi-Graphical Model (GmGM) framework, which jointly infers cell-cell and gene-gene dependency structure from a single scRNA-seq data matrix, to a 10x Genomics PBMC dataset. Ten independent GMGM-Leiden clustering runs were integrated into a robust consensus partition using a soft cluster ensemble approach and benchmarked against reference cell-type annotations. This strategy yielded stable cluster partitions that resolve biologically meaningful sub-populations not distinguished by the reference annotation. In parallel, for each cluster, gene co-expression modules were extracted from the fitted model via consensus Leiden clustering across resolutions, evaluated using standard network metrics, and validated functionally with the Network Enrichment Analysis Test (NEAT), which confirmed non-random enrichment signal. A module-scoring procedure linked network topology to per-cell, per-cluster expression signatures, and a novel extension of GmGM, recovering a shared cell-cell network together with population-specific gene networks in a single model run, was demonstrated in a case study on the CD4+ T-cell population. These results indicate that GmGM provides a unified, reproducible framework for joint cell clustering and gene-network inference, capable of revealing cellular structure beyond that captured by conventional pipelines.

new_today.title: Topologically-based parameter inference for agent-based model selection from spatiotemporal cellular data
new_today.title_zh: 基于拓扑的参数推断用于时空细胞数据的基于代理模型选择
new_today.summary_zh: 时空单细胞成像的进展使得详细观察细胞群体动态和细胞间相互作用成为可能。然而，将这些丰富数据集转化为机制洞察仍是重大挑战。基于代理模型（ABMs）是一种自下而上的计算框架，用于研究由单个相邻细胞间相互作用规则产生的细胞群体涌现行为，而拓扑数据分析（TDA）提供空间组织的稳健描述符。我们提出TOPAZ（基于拓扑的参数推断用于基于代理模型优化），一个将TDA与近似贝叶斯计算（ABC）、近似近似贝叶斯计算（AABC）和贝叶斯模型选择相结合的计算流程，从时空细胞数据中识别生物学合理的ABMs。TOPAZ使用持续同调量化细胞轨迹的空间特征，并通过ABC和AABC结合拓扑信息进行参数推断，使用贝叶斯信息准则进行模型比较。我们使用成纤维细胞集体运动模拟验证TOPAZ，展示其准确恢复模型参数并区分基线ABM和包含对齐相互作用的扩展模型的能力。我们的结果和开源代码展示了TOPAZ作为空间单细胞分析中机制推断和

extra.description: Advances in spatiotemporal single-cell imaging have enabled detailed observations of cell population dynamics and intercellular interactions. However, translating these rich data sets into mechanistic insight remains a significant challenge. Agent-based models (ABMs) are a bottom-up computational framework for investigating the emergent behavior of cell populations that can arise from rules defining the interactions between individual neighboring cells, while topological data analysis (TDA) provides robust descriptors of spatial organization. We present TOPAZ (TOpologically-based Parameter inference for Agent-based model optimiZation), a computational pipeline that integrates TDA with approximate Bayesian computation (ABC), approximate approximate Bayesian computation (AABC), and Bayesian model selection to identify biologically plausible ABMs from spatiotemporal cellular data. TOPAZ uses persistent homology to quantify spatial features of cell trajectories and combines this topological information with parameter inference via ABC and AABC and model comparison using the Bayesian information criterion. We validate TOPAZ using simulations of collective fibroblast movement, demonstrating its ability to accurately recover model parameters and distinguish between a baseline ABM and an extended model that incorporates an alignment interaction. Our results and open-source code demonstrate the utility of TOPAZ as an extensible framework for mechanistic inference and model discrimination in spatial single-cell analysis.
